recognition.text: Official ESA/Hubble press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: This Hubble image shows NGC 6388, a globular cluster in the Milky Way. Like all globular clusters, it formed long ago and is more than ten billion years old. Even so, astronomers describe it as dynamically middle-aged.

The distinction is between calendar age and internal evolution. Over time, the heaviest stars in a cluster gradually sink toward its center. By studying how the cluster's bright blue stars are spread out, researchers found that NGC 6388 has aged at a moderate pace, with its heaviest stars still in the middle of that migration.

Those bright blue stars are blue stragglers, stars that look younger than their neighbors. A study using Hubble data showed that globulars of matching age may have very different distributions of blue stragglers, which suggests that clusters can age at substantially different rates.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (3.56 x 3.49 arcminutes) and distance (35000 light years), the frame spans roughly 36 × 36 light-years. Its light set out about 35,000 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This image comes from Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys, using blue, visible and near-infrared filters. The color assigned to each filter isn't published.
understand.eye: The near-infrared light is invisible to the eye, and Hubble's sharp view separates stars that would otherwise blur together.
